html:
The siege of Constantinople in the summer of 626 by the Avars and their Slavic subjects, while a Persian army waited across the Bosporus. It came at the height of the last great war with Persia, when the emperor Heraclius was away fighting in the Caucasus.

The Avar khagan attacked the land walls with siege engines for about ten days. The Persian general Shahrbaraz held the Asian shore, and the plan was for Slav canoes to ferry Persian troops across. The Roman fleet sank the canoes, the land attacks failed, and the Avars pulled back. The city was led by the patriarch Sergius and the official Bonus. Its people credited their victory to the Virgin Mary, whose icon had been carried along the walls.

The failure saved the empire. Avar power began to fade, and the next year Heraclius beat the Persians in Mesopotamia, forcing peace in 628.
